text:
maria.k: Heads-up: saw a spike in soft-429s on /v1/generate after yesterday's runtime kernel hint change. Not huge in count but correlated with a 12% p95 latency increase for short-chat workloads.

ajay: ugh, saw that in the alert. Which fleet/region?

maria.k: us-west-2 dedicated pool A (gpu-x). Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/2808 (ops-only).

kevin: perf-bot ran sampling traces after the deploy, posting summary now.

perf-bot: sample summary: 1) batch formation shifted leading to more micro-batches (~30% increase in 1-2 request batches) 2) kv-cache hit ratio stable 3) switch to kernel-v2 favored long-seq kernels for small sequences -> increased kernel switch overhead. (attached: flame snippet)

lee: Interesting — increased micro-batches would blow up per-request overhead. Did the batcher prefetch/buffer window shrink in the change?

maria.k: batch_window_ms was reduced from 6 -> 4 in the hint PR (to lower tail for long seqs). It probably made sense overall but hit short-chat.

ajay: Can we confirm token budget per-admit changed? I thought we left token_budget_target intact.

kevin: token_budget_target is the same, but admission code uses kernel-hint to choose admission path. If kernel-v2 detects small sequence it still routes to long-kernel fallback path due to a heuristic bug. That causes an extra kernel swap which blocks the batcher for ~1.8ms and causes some queue timeouts -> soft-429s.

maria.k: repro script I ran:
```
# replay short-chat load
wrk -t8 -d60s -c200 --script=short_chat.lua http://api-redwood/v1/generate
```
kevin: good repro. I also grabbed a brief profile (perf/trace) showing kernel_switch ms spikes in the hot path.

perf-bot: small excerpt (top events):
- batch_assemble: +45% CPU
- kernel_switch: median 1.8ms -> 3.6ms on affected nodes
- kv_cache_lookup: no regression

lee: two-pronged plan: 1) hotfix admit path to prefer the previous kernel-selection heuristic for sequences < 64 tokens (revert the kernel hint decision table), 2) temporary raise soft-limit slack (increase admission grace tokens) to avoid soft-429s while we validate.

ajay: For (2) can we do a config flip? I can push an emergency flag to dedicated pools: `admit.soft_budget_slack=1.5` (default 1.0) and `batch_window_ms=6` for us-west-2 only.

maria.k: please do the config flip first, small blast radius. Then Kevin can land a guarded revert-ish patch that keeps long-seq wins but preserves old path for short sequences.

kevin: I'll open a tiny PR: change is minimal, adding explicit check: `if tokens < 64 -> prefer kernel-v1 path` and add a metric `admit.kernel_mismatch_count`. Will run canary on 2 nodes.

lee: also we should add a quick perf test to the rollout pipeline: `short-chat` suite at 200 qps for 60s and fail on >5% soft-429s or p95 regressed >8%.

maria.k: agree. Action items: ajay flip config (in 10m), kevin PR + canary, lee add pipeline test, I'll monitor dashboards and call SRE if we see >50 soft-429s/min.

ajay: flipping config now to us-west-2:dpool-A -> setting `admit.soft_budget_slack=1.5`, `batch_window_ms=6`. Pushing change.

perf-bot: config change applied to 3 nodes in us-west-2:dpool-A (2026-03-18T15:12Z). Observed soft-429 rate dropping within 30s.

maria.k: nice. kevin — want me to hold the revert until your canary finishes?

kevin: yes hold. I'll post canary results in this thread. Preliminary local canary looks good: kernel_switch med down to ~1.9ms, micro-batch rate normalized.

lee: follow-up: add a dedicated metric for `batch_size_distribution` in telemetry so next time we can quickly detect micro-batch drift. Also add an alert for median kernel_switch > 2.5ms.

kevin: noted. I'll add `admit.kernel_mismatch_count` and `runtime.kernel_switch_ms` and update docs for kernel-hint caveats.

maria.k: thanks team. We'll keep this thread updated. If anyone sees regressions elsewhere (eu, apac) ping me.

kevin: can we also check fallback path cost? If fallback kernel is expensive, we might want to early-eject requests to dedicated cheap-kernel replicas rather than do kernel swap on the same worker. Filing follow-up ticket.

ajay: filed RED-8123: "Prefer routing to cheap-kernel replicas before in-place kernel swap for small sequences".

maria.k: closing loop for now — feel free to DM if something pops. :thumbsup:
